concepts.why: The presence of an intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells, positive for CK7 and EMA, is consistent with Extramammary Paget's disease.
The presence of numerous reactive dendritic HMB-45–positive melanocytes scattered among tumor cells suggests a possible diagnosis of Malignant melanoma.
The initial presentation of a small eczematous, pink-to-brown plaque, which later changed to a dark brown color, could be consistent with Seborrheic keratosis.
The presence of an enlarged and variegated plaque with well-demarcated margins could be consistent with Dermatofibroma.
The presence of an intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells could also be consistent with Basal cell carcinoma.
It explains the presence of pagetoid cells with round, pale vacuolated cytoplasm and large pleomorphic nuclei in the histopathology findings.
